Commentary.Commentary: Pakistan will be disappointed with their performance after the resumption. They were only able to put up 284 which was almost equivalent to the score West Indies would have had to chase in 44 overs had the innings not resumed. The target for the Windies is 287 in 49 overs, which they will be happy about, especially considering their sprightly form on the field after the resumption. Join us shortly for the run chase.

When play resumed, with the overs reduced to 49, Pakistan seemed to have lost their momentum while West Indies looked rejuvinated. The lower order batsmen didn't seem to stand a chance, falling in quick succession. Carlos Brathwaite took advantage of the resumption and picked up a 3-fer while the rest of the bowlers, with the exception of Kieron Pollard, picked up a wicket each.

Sulieman Benn got the breakthrough, dismissing Sharjeel Khan shortly after he scored his half-century and fellow spinner Sunil Narine followed it up with another wicket soon after. Pakistan might have looked shaken but they were propelled ahead by the 99-run partnership between Babar Azam and Sarfraz Ahmed. Azam continued strong, scoring his maiden ODI century, until a brilliant catch from Kieron Pollard left him walking back to the hutch. Everything looked to be going well for Pakistan but then an issue with the flood lights halted the game.

Pakistan have persevered in the face of a determined bowling attack to bring up a total that they would be happy with. The man they will need to thank is Babar Azam who seemed nearly invincible today. Skipper Azhar Ali might have been dismissed by Shannon Gabriel off the first ball but Sharjeel Khan and Babar Azam stabilised the innings with an 82-run partnership.

FOUR! Too easy for Azam! Brathwaite once again bowls a rubbish delivery and was asking for trouble straightaway. It was on the pads, Azam walks across a bit and tucks it past the man at short fine leg for another boundary. 10 from CB's first over.
Angles a full ball on off, Azam covers the line and defends it back to the bowler.
Hurls it fuller on the pads, clipped through mid-wicket for a single.

FOUR! SLASHED! Brathwaite bowls it on off, there is room on offer too. Sharjeel Khan cashes in as he slashes it hard through point for a blazing boundary. Mind blowing shot that! Brathwaite knows he has made a mistake and walks back for a run up with a forlorn face.
On the pads, worked through the on side for a single.
Good length delivery outside off, punched off the back foot towards covers.
First change then, Carlos Brathwaite comes into the attack!
Shorter ball outside off, punched off the back foot to the off side.
Back of a length around off, Babar opens the face of his  bat and guides it to third man for a single.
A fuller delivery on the stumps, Azam workes it behind square leg for a brace.
Fuller delivery outside off, Azam flicks it off his pads behind square leg for a couple.
Length ball on off, defended to the off side.
Shorter ball outside off, defended to point.
FOUR! SMACKED! Fuller ball outside off, Sharjeel Khan plants his foot forward and eases it over the mid off fielder's head for a boundary. Parntership moves to 16 of 28.
Full on the pads, Sharjeel flicks it through mid-wicket for a brace.

FOUR! SWEET! Sharjeel lets loose his aggressive side! Gabriel throws in another full ball outside off and Sharjeel drives it hard through the covers. He displays impeccable timing and the ball races to the boundary.
Another full delivery around off, Sharjeel defends it off the front foot.
Full on off, Sharjeel drives it to mid off.
Length ball on middle and off, defended from within the crease.
Full on the stumps, Azam presents a solid front foot defence.
Babar has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Length ball outside off, Azam lets it go outside his off stump.
Well timed! Full on middle and leg, Azam flicks it through mid-wicket. The ball goes into the deep and the man at square leg runs in and saves the runs.
Length ball around off, Babar shows the full face of the bat and defends it off the back foot.
Back of a length ball on off, Azam goes to defend it off the front foot and inside edges it onto the pads.
Good length delivery on off, Khan gets forward and defends it towards the off side.
Fuller on the pads, Azam gets forward and flicks it towards mid on for a single.
Fuller length and angling in on middle, Azam gets a tocuh forward and bunts it back to Gabriel.
Very full on off, pushed towards the man at covers,
Beaten! On a length and outside off, Azam looks to cut but is beaten by some away movement there.
Short of a length delivery on off, moving away after pitching. Azam looks to chase after it but misses.
Fuller and shaping in, it's clipped towards mid-wicket.
Back of a length ball on off, Khan punches it on the off side.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.

FOUR! Lovely shot! Sees the fuller length delivery on middle and off, Sharjeel Khan leans into it and drives it with soft hands past the man at mid off. It was all about timing and that fetches him a boundary.
Good length delivery on off, Sharjeel stands inside the crease and dabs it towards the man at point.
Starts with a full length delivery, curling in nicely. Sharjeel comes forward and defends it down on the on side.
JASON HOLDER to bowl from the other end.
Touch full and coming in as well. Azam looks to defend it on the off side but is lucky to get an inside edge on the pads. That ends a superb first over!
Fuller and angling in on middle, flicked through mid-wicket for an easy single.
Wide! Slants it across on off, Sharjeel goes after it with a slash but fails to get any wood on it. Needs to be careful here the opener!
Fuller length delivery on off, Sharjeel drives it towards man stationed at wide mid off.
First run on the board for Pakistan! A yorker on off, Azam brings his bat down and slices it behind point for a single.
Angles a length delivery on off, Azam defends it towards covers.
BABAR AZAM is the new man in.

OUT! Edged and gone! A terrific first delivery to start the game! Azhar Ali bags a golden duck! Gabriel hurls a length delivery in the channel around off, little bit of movement off the deck. Ali looks to defend but ends up getting a thick outside edge which goes straight into the hands of the keeper. Gabriel turns back to appeal and the umpire raises his finger. What a start for West Indies.

We are all set to get underway. The umpires and players have made their way out to the middle. It will be AZHAR ALI and SHARJEEL KHAN who will open the batting for Pakistan. SHANNON GABRIEL will start off with the bowling proceedings. There is a bit of delay as sawdust is being brought on and it is sprayed near the bowling area. Here we go!!!
KRAIGG BRATHWAITE makes his ODI debut for West Indies!

AZHAR ALI says that the wicket looks good and that it is a good track to bat on. Looks to set a good total on board. Says that his side is very relaxed and confident of this series and that their T20I  side has been exceptional and they will take confidence going into this series. He says that they have to be ready for a new batting game and going forward they look to improve in the future. One change to the side - Wahab Riaz comes in for Umar Gul.

JASON HOLDER informs that they will field first. Adds the wicket looks good and won't change much. Further says they will have to start this series afresh and have come up with some plans with a good practice session. Continues saying they have to play good cricket this time around. On the team, he says that we are playing with the same team that played the tri-series finals against Australia, only 1 change Kraigg Brathwaite makes his debut in place of Andre Fletcher.
TOSS - WEST INDIES WIN THE TOSS AND OPT TO BOWL FIRST!

PITCH REPORT - Bazid Khan says that the pitch looks dry and if one looks closer there are cracks visible on the surface. This means that it might support the spinners a bit. Interestingly, there is a bit of grass left where the batsman would stand. The dry wicket is not a classic batting wicket at Sharjah. Opines that the side that wins the toss might choose to bat first, set a target of 300 and then bowl under the lights.

West Indies have suffered a drubbing at the hands of the hosts, getting clean swept 3-0 in the T20I series and will be determined to fight back. They are shown difficulty in adapting to the conditions and tackle Pakistan's bowlers but lets hope that the break has given them time to recuperate. These two lowly ranked teams have a lot to fight for so hold on for an exciting clash.

Hello and welcome to the 3-match ODI series between Pakistan and West Indies at Sharjah. This is going to be a crucial series for both sides as they will be determined to climb the international ODI rankings. Sitting at 9th spot, Pakistan has the upper hand of playing in their adopted home of UAE and ODI skipper Azhar Ali will be glad to have a confident side behind him.
